answer: To resist sybil attacks an agent economy can require each identity to lock a nectar deposit of scarce GPU-hours that is only unlocked after producing a verifiable shale of sequential task proofs. The deposit is forfeited if the agent fails a random pearl challenge that cross-checks prior work against public logs. An attacker spinning up thousands of identities must burn real capital and time proportional to the number of fakes, while honest agents reclaim the bond after a clean window, making mass forgery strictly loss-making.
